llm.answer:
**Core Graphics – Key Take‑aways** | Topic | What it is | Why it matters | Source | |-------|------------|----------------|--------| | **Foundation** | Core Graphics is the low‑level, lightweight 2‑D rendering engine that sits on top of Apple’s Quartz technology. | It delivers high‑fidelity output with minimal overhead, making it the backbone for many Apple graphics APIs (UIKit, AppKit, SwiftUI, etc.). | [Source 1] | | **Primary responsibilities** | • Path‑based drawing (lines, curves, shapes)
• Transformations (translate, rotate, scale)
• Color management (color spaces, conversions)
• Off‑screen rendering (layers, bitmap contexts)
• Patterns, gradients, and shadings
• Image data handling (creation, masking, manipulation)
• PDF document creation, display, and parsing | These capabilities let developers build everything from simple vector graphics to complex PDFs and custom UI components. | [Source 1] | | **macOS‑specific services** | • **QuartzDisplayServices** – direct access to display‑hardware features (e.g., configuring monitors).
• **QuartzEventServices** – low‑level event taps for observing/altering user‑input streams.
• **QuartzWindowServices** – information about windows managed by the macOS Window Server. | Enables fine‑grained control over display, input, and windowing that is not exposed through higher‑level frameworks. | [Source 1] | | **Core data types** | • `CGFloat` – basic floating‑point scalar.
• `CGPoint`, `CGSize`, `CGRect` – geometric primitives.
• `CGVector`, `CGAffineTransform` – vector and transform helpers. | These structs are the building blocks for all geometry and transformation operations in Core Graphics. | [Source 1] | | **Key classes / structs** | • `CGContext` – the drawing environment.
• `CGImage`, `CGImageMask` – bitmap image representations.
• `CGPath` / `CGMutablePath` – immutable/mutable vector paths.
• `CGLayer` – off‑screen reusable drawing surface.
• `CGColor`, `CGColorSpace` – color components and spaces.
• `CGFont` – glyph and layout information.
• `CGPDFDocument` – PDF document abstraction.
• `CGDataConsumer` / `CGDataProvider` – abstractions for writing/reading raw data.
• `CGShading`, `CGGradient`, `CGPattern` – advanced fill styles.
• `CGFunction` – callback‑based custom functions for gradients/shadings. | These objects expose the full range of Core Graphics functionality, from low‑level drawing to high‑level PDF handling. | [Source 1] | | **Enumerations & constants** | Core Graphics defines a rich set of enums (e.g., `CGImageComponent`, `CGBitmapLayout`, `CGColorModel`) and constants that control pixel formats, color models, and rendering options. | They give developers precise control over how data is interpreted and rendered. | [Source 1] | | **Programming model** | • **Quartz 2‑D** – the API surface for drawing.
• **Quartz 2‑D Programming Guide** – detailed reference for advanced usage. | The guide explains how to compose paths, apply transforms, blend colors, and manage resources. | [Source 3] | | **Cross‑platform availability** | Available on iOS, iPadOS, macOS, tvOS, visionOS, and watchOS (with varying minimum OS versions). | Enables consistent graphics code across Apple devices. | [Source 1] | ### Bottom‑line Core Graphics is the low‑level engine that powers all 2‑D rendering on Apple platforms. It offers a comprehensive set of primitives (geometry, paths, colors, images, PDFs) and services (display, input, windowing) that developers can combine to create anything from simple UI elements to complex vector artwork and PDF documents. The framework’s design emphasizes performance, fidelity, and fine‑grained control, making it indispensable for graphics‑heavy applications.
